lines.text: Why can you hear someone speaking around a corner even when you cannot see them? A wave can spread into a region beyond an opening or edge.

Diffraction means the spreading of waves as they pass through an aperture or around the edge of an obstacle. Plane waves reaching a narrow gap emerge as curved wavefronts that spread into the shadow region. Diffraction is a wave phenomenon and occurs for water waves, sound and light. The wave does not need a new medium, it can spread while its speed, frequency and wavelength remain unchanged.
This builds on wavelength and wavefronts. The spacing between consecutive crests can stay the same even while the wavefronts change direction and curve around an edge.
Diffraction, spreading of waves through a gap or around an edge. Wavefronts curve into the region beyond the barrier. It is a wave behaviour, not a change of medium.
What two parts must a complete definition of diffraction include?

Which observation shows diffraction? A wave reflects from a wall. A wave spreads beyond the edge of a barrier. A wave slows in a new medium. Two waves overlap. B Spreading around an obstacle edge is diffraction.
A ripple tank lets you see how the same waves behave at wide and narrow gaps. The visible change is the angle through which the wavefronts spread.

Use a vibrating straight bar to produce plane water waves in a ripple tank. Place a barrier with a gap across their path and observe the waves before and after it. The emerging wavefronts curve and spread, this demonstrates diffraction. Compare gap width w with wavelength lambda, the spacing of adjacent crests. Spreading is pronounced when w is comparable with lambda, when w is much wider, the spread is smaller. At fixed water depth, speed is approximately constant. The vibrator fixes frequency, so passing through the gap leaves speed, frequency and wavelength unchanged. To increase spreading, narrow the gap or, at constant depth, lower the frequency, v equals f lambda then gives a larger wavelength.
Use v equals f lambda from progressive waves to reason about changing frequency. The key comparison is wavelength relative to gap width, not amplitude.

Make plane waves with a straight vibrator, direct them through a gap. Wavefronts spread more when gap width is comparable with wavelength. Widening the gap reduces the spread at fixed wavelength. At unchanged depth, the gap does not change wavelength.
If the gap widens at fixed water depth and vibrator frequency, what happens to the spread and wavelength?

A gap is much wider than the water wave wavelength. Which change makes spreading more obvious? Widen the gap. Increase amplitude. Narrow the gap. Increase water depth without any other information. C Narrowing the gap makes its width closer to the wavelength, so the wave spreads more.

A sound wave of wavelength zero point five zero metres passes through a doorway of width one point zero metres between two rooms. Which change increases the amount of diffraction that takes place?
Halving frequency doubles wavelength to one point zero metres, matching the doorway. Increasing amplitude changes size, not spread, widening the doorway reduces diffraction.

Water waves of wavelength lambda are incident normally on an obstacle with a narrow gap. The width of the gap is equal to lambda. The waves from the gap emerge over an angle theta as shown. The gap is slowly widened. Which changes, if any, occur to theta and to the wavelength of the emerging waves?
As the gap widens relative to wavelength, theta decreases. The same medium means the wavelength stays unchanged, B reverses the angular trend.

Water waves of wavelength lambda are incident normally on an obstacle with a narrow gap. The width of the gap is equal to lambda. The waves from the gap emerge over an angle theta, as shown. The gap is slowly widened. Which changes, if any, occur to theta and to the wavelength of the emerging waves?
A wider gap produces less spreading, so theta decreases without changing wavelength. B was popular but assumes wider gaps cause more diffraction.
A light wave passes through a single slit and a diffraction pattern forms. What happens to the frequency and the speed of the wave when it is diffracted?
Diffraction in the same medium changes direction distribution, not frequency or speed. C incorrectly assumes speed decreases.

An electromagnetic wave is diffracted as it passes through a single slit. The width of the slit is larger than the wavelength of the wave. Which change will decrease the amount of diffraction of the wave?
Decreasing period increases frequency, reducing wavelength at fixed speed and therefore reducing diffraction. C makes the slit narrower and increases spreading.
A teacher is explaining diffraction to a group of students. Which piece of apparatus is most appropriate for the teacher to use to demonstrate diffraction?

In which situation does diffraction occur?
Passing through a gap can make a wave spread. A describes reflection, a different behaviour.
A water wave in a ripple tank is diffracted as it passes through a gap in a barrier. Which two factors affect the angle of diffraction of the wave?
The ratio of wavelength to gap width controls spreading. Amplitude changes wave height, not the angle.
What is meant by diffraction?
Diffraction is spreading around an edge. D describes superposition and does not require an edge.
Which waves would best demonstrate diffraction through a doorway?

A water wave passes through a gap in a harbour wall and diffracts. The gap has a width of eight metres. The wave travels directly towards the gap. For which wavelength is the diffraction of the wave greatest?
A wavelength equal to the eight metres gap gives the greatest spreading among these options. The one metre wave is much shorter and spreads less.

eight point two Diffraction.
In one breath.
Diffraction is the spreading of waves as they pass through an aperture or around the edge of an obstacle. The spreading is most obvious when the aperture width is comparable with the wavelength.
Key ideas.

A plane wave approaching a barrier travels straight until it reaches an opening. After the opening, the wavefronts spread into the region that would otherwise be in the barrier's shadow. This is diffraction. The same effect occurs around a single edge. It is a behaviour of waves, including water waves, sound and light.

The comparison that matters is the wavelength lambda relative to the gap width w. When w is of the same order as lambda, the emerging wavefronts can be strongly curved and the wave spreads through a large angle. When w is much greater than lambda, most of each wavefront continues almost straight, with noticeable bending only near the edges. A narrower gap, at unchanged wavelength, gives a larger spread. Diffraction can occur at other widths too, comparable describes when it is particularly easy to observe.

Figure, Ripple tank wavefronts after passing through gaps wider than, comparable with, and narrower than the wavelength, compare the spread while the crest spacing stays similar. source, nine seven zero two c8.2, p.5. Notice how the outgoing crests become more curved as the gap narrows, measure crest spacing along the direction of wave travel.

The marked crest to crest distance is the wavelength lambda to compare with gap width in the ripple tank figure. This displacement distance graph shows a side profile at one instant, the ripple tank photographs show the crests from above. Both views represent the same wavelength. See OpenStax, wavefront and side profile comparison.

A barrier does not change the medium. If the water depth stays the same, the wave speed stays approximately constant. The source sets the frequency, which also remains constant across the gap. Thus v equals f lambda tells us that the wavelength before and after the gap is unchanged. Changing the gap width changes the shape and direction of the wavefronts, not the spacing between successive crests.
Method.
In a ripple tank, use a vibrating straight bar to make approximately plane water waves.
Put a barrier with one gap across their path. Observe the wavefronts before and after the barrier, ideally from above with a lamp or projected image.
Compare the gap width with the measured spacing of successive crests, the wavelength. Adjust the gap until its width is comparable with the wavelength and look for curved wavefronts beyond it.

Widen the gap while keeping the water depth and vibrator frequency fixed. The spreading angle decreases. Alternatively, lower the frequency at constant depth. Since v equals f lambda, the wavelength rises and spreading increases through a fixed gap.
Worked example.

Sound of frequency four hundred and forty hertz travels at three hundred and thirty metres per second towards a doorway zero point eight zero metres wide. Predict whether diffraction is pronounced. Use v equals f lambda, then lambda equals v over f. Substitute, lambda equals three hundred and thirty over four hundred and forty equals zero point seven five metres. This wavelength is close to the zero point eight zero metres gap width, so the sound spreads appreciably through the doorway.
Traps.
Trap, A wider gap gives a wider spread. Why it's wrong, A wider gap is larger relative to the same wavelength. Instead, Compare w with lambda, widening the gap reduces spreading.
Trap, Passing through a gap changes the wavelength. Why it's wrong, The medium and frequency have not changed. Instead, Draw the outgoing crests at the same spacing, although they curve.

Trap, Increasing wave amplitude increases the diffraction angle. Why it's wrong, Amplitude describes wave size, not its wavelength to gap ratio. Instead, Change wavelength or gap width to change the spread.
Exam technique.

For Define, say spreading of waves and name a gap or edge. For a ripple tank Describe question, give the source, barrier and gap, then state what is observed beyond the gap. For Explain or Predict questions, compare wavelength with gap width and mention any constant depth or speed before using v equals f lambda. Never claim the gap changes the wavelength by itself.
